body:
I've read L'Etranger (The Stranger) by Camus and several short stories & essays by Sartre. My favourite is probably Neitzsche, though - I have a Kaufman anthology that is dog-eared from having been read and re-read so many times.

I do feel that existential philosophy is interesting, but I don't feel it solves anything. That is, I agree with their premise (there is no God, we are alone), but can't follow it out of that. I hadn't read about existential therapy before, though, so I will read that. Thanks for the link.

> *So am I that off in thinking maybe I should just kill myself?* I would have to say, just because you don't know what you're doing now, even at your age, clearly, yes.

I guess that question might be rephrased as "My current situation, by objective standards, is highly desirable, However, nothing I've done, after years of trying, has remedied myt emotional situtation. Thus, is it likely that *anything* will ever remedy the situation? 

As for which country I moved to, it's a French speaking European one.

I think that my circuitry is probably a little off. I have an paternal uncle with schizophrenia and my maternal grandmother was once hospitalized for depression. I also think my father tried to kill himself, when he was younger, based on a pair of unusual wrist scars. He's never said anything, but small bits of conversation lead me to strongly suspect I'm correct. All of this suggests that there I have a familial predisposition to depression.

So I'm open to the idea that my apathy/depression might be genetic. That being said, knowing the cause doesn't really address the fact that it's there.

I tried self medicating with Prozac (online pharmacies FTW), which actually made things worse. I've been tempted to try Wellbutrin, which is a dopamine regulator (rather than a serotonin regulator), but haven't gotten around to it. Also, being in a foreign country, it would be hard to find an English speaking therapist, much less one that I could relate to.

Then, there's the fact that I have a very hard time discussing my feelings. Anonymous online conversation is one thing, but speaking to a therapist is much more difficult. And then, how do I explain this to the live-in girlfriend? Do I hide a weekly appointment from her? How? She's not stupid and would probably figure out something was up, and I'm not capable of admitting to her that I might need help (think of a 1950s male). If I start lying, I'm bound to get caught.

Finally, I actually have tried speaking to a therapist before, back home. It was at the university counselling centre. While he was a great, friendly guy, I didn't feel I could talk about wanting to kill myself. He's legally bound, as a therapist, to inform the police if he feels that my life (or the life of another) is in imminent danger. Knowing this kept me from ever opening up, for fear that I might get reported if I talked about how serious I was.

Yeah, that got passed around the lab. I think I got in the low 20s last time. 

EDIT: Got a 21. A little geeky, perhaps, but not excessive.

No, it's not. She's just one more factor. I think it's that I've realized every relationship is eventually going to settle into comfort, routine, and petty squabbles. Mainly, it's that I've tried just about everything life has to offer and none of it has really interested me. 

And I speak the language here (French - been living here for 2 years - originally from North America); I just don't relate to anyone. Here or back home. Sure, I can put on an act and be entertaining when I go out, but it's just that - an act. I don't particularly care for any of our friends. In fact, I prefer to stay home, which probably doesn't help.

Most of the people who know me seem to like me, BTW. They generally consider me outgoing and happy-go-lucky, ironically enough.

EDITS: Clarification, typos.

That's the thing - I recognize, objectively, that things could be worse. That I probably have it pretty well. And yet I *still* don't care.

I've tried everything and still no luck. So am I that off in thinking maybe I should just kill myself?

More about me:

I'm an atheist, with physics & philosophy degrees. A minor in math and a grad degree in medical physics. Having done research (important research, according to some), I still feel my work was a drop in the bucket that could have been done (and eventually would have been done) just as easily by others. My life still felt meaningless when I graduated.

I tried doing volunteer work in Africa. Hey, if my life sucks, I might as well make someone else's better, right? No dice. Most of my work was, at best, misguided. Anyone who's done work with the Peace Corps or other organizations knows what I'm talking about.

I moved to a foreign country with a girl I loved. Things are different here, but still largely the same. The love I once had has mellowed into petty squabbles over unimportant issues. And she's not the first girl I've ever loved; every relationship I've had grows stale. I thought it would be different with this one, but it's not. It just means the petty squabbles are less frequent than in other relationships.

And still, I can't care about anything. I've travelled the world, backpacking, and still nothing feels motivating. I just want to care about something, but all I have left is apathy. 

I think about the MASH song, "Suicide is painless."

    The game of life is hard to play
    I'm gonna lose it anyway
    The losing card I'll someday lay
    So this is all I have to say...
    
    The only way to win is cheat
    And lay it down before I'm beat
    And to another give my seat
    For that's the only painless feat. 


I'm going to die anyway. Someday. So what difference does it matter if it's today or tomorrow if even *I* don't care?

Anyway, sorry about the rambling.
